entries.reason: Roku local storage and background transfer are not a governed first-public capability.
entries.followUp: Reopen only with a versioned Roku storage and lifecycle contract.

entries.reason: AirPlay is an Apple platform capability and is not a Roku receiver contract.
entries.followUp: No Roku action until an approved receiver authority exists.

entries.reason: Roku does not provide the reviewed Cast receiver boundary used by the Apple clients.
entries.followUp: Reopen with a signed receiver and typed handoff contract.

entries.reason: The Roku playback lifecycle has no approved PiP ownership model.
entries.followUp: Reopen with background playback, focus, and grant-lifecycle evidence.

entries.reason: Roku caption appearance is governed by OS-level settings rather than an app-owned style model.
entries.followUp: Audio Guide and low-vision hardware acceptance must verify the system path.

entries.reason: The reviewed Roku Video contract does not expose a safe variable-rate authority.
entries.followUp: Reopen only after decoder and progress semantics are versioned.

entries.reason: Roku source code publishes a conservative profile and does not invent decoder tuples.
entries.followUp: Replace with measured tuples only through the protected capability probe process.

entries.reason: Roku exposes fewer app-level motion controls; player transitions must remain bounded and skippable.
entries.followUp: Verify Audio Guide, motion, and focus behavior on hardware.

entries.reason: Unknown required routes cannot be guessed; optional capabilities may be ignored without widening authority.
entries.followUp: Add a registry entry before introducing a new cross-client route.
